questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The availability of behavioral and experimental economics courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - the exchange arrival team was very helpful

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The exchange arrival team provides all details

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Yes super easy using the OeAD website.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Definitely look at the district that the student dorm is located in rather than the aerial distance to your faculty

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I found my housing at ViennaBase 19 which is a student dorm through the OeAD website which is extremely easy to navigate. However later I learnt that the price mentioned in the website was 50 euros per month more than what is being charged to some other students who booked directly on the ViennaBase 19 website. 

Also, I chose this dorm since distance-wise it was close to the University with a tram available doorstep to doorstep. However in retrospect I have realised that in Vienna the aerial distance doesn't matter. What matters is the district you live in: the closer to the inner city you are, the better it is: people are more friendly and welcoming to outsiders who can't speak German fluently.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
So there are two systems of point allocation and preference ranking depending on the faculty you are in. I was in the Economics and business faculty which had the complicated point allocation system. 

Also while the courses themselves aren't at a high level as KU, the ECTS number allocated for each course is lower so people have to do at least 4-6 courses if they want 30 ECTS and that can get hectic.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Looking into the University's webpages, I found an explanation of the system. I asked my assigned buddy for help on what strategy to use.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful in getting the courses I got the pre-approval for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The strategy is that two hours before the Registeration closes, it is recommended to go and allocate maximum points to the courses where there is demand (>500 points) and almost none (i.e. between 1-10 points) to courses were there are still empty places. Since all students do this, ensure that you aren't doing it in the last minute as the system is widely-known to crash. 

Also unlike KU, you can actually go to the first class and then drop it if not interested. This means you can sign up for more classes than required.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I'm on my final year of Masters - by the time I went to University of Vienna, I only had my Master thesis left to do back in KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Entirely dependent on the professor - some of them are chill and interactive while some others are formal. You can get the vibe from the course description and first day of class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Topics in Behavioural Economics - a Seminar 
VCEE seminar series 
International negotiations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The international negotiations is hands-down the best course I have attended - the professor was extremely interactive and insightful and we did case studies and role-playing of practical scenarios like job negotiations which is useful outside of the university. 

Will also recommend the other courses I took as they were also interesting and provided additional perspective to what I have learnt at KU.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was fined once 50 euros in public transport for having my mask in my hand and not wearing it as soon as I entered. So be prepared to follow the rules to the letter

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Generally, food and other items are less expensive than here. However there are so many interesting museums and arts and culture so do budget for that :D

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is extremely competitive to get into the sports classes at University. However there are plenty more opportunities apart from sports. I was in a book club and the university poetry writing club and made some great friends via it

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are so many activities being conducted by the exchange team so definitely look out for that. To meet local students, recommend joining some club of interest like mentioned above

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are so many arts and culture activities happening throughout the city which are still accessible to students on a budget

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it was fairly easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are no concepts of study groups. However people are generally friendly if you take the first step to go talk to them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Outside of University and tourist areas, people don't know as much English and hence learning some basic German is recommended. People of color might also face some looks in some areas so do check the route in advance to wherever you are going.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very relaxed - they read newspapers and physical books in the trams and take long coffee breaks

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Everything mentioned above - I think it's a great city to live in both in summer and winter and offers a different culture while still providing the same infrastructure as Copenhagen: perhaps one will miss biking as Vienna is a bigger city

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything mentioned above

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The culture of the city and classes at university and the discussions in it

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Nothing much really - everything fairly runs smoothly like here. If you are vegetarian or vegan then there might be difficulties as not many places have the option like here. Also if you are super environmentally-conscious then you would be appalled by the lack of recycling available there

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
